category: XSim Advanced Usage, Netlist/Timing Simulation & Third-Party Simulators
description: Beyond the basic compile/elaborate/run flow: the remaining xsim Tcl commands (waveform organisation, breakpoints and stepping, value inspection, VCD/SAIF logging, tracing), xelab/xsim command-line options for DPI, timing simulation, libraries and coverage, project-mode simulation settings (filesets, generics, defines, xsim.* properties), post-synthesis and post-implementation simulation, and how Vivado hands a design to Questa/ModelSim, VCS, Xcelium and Riviera-PRO.

tools.name: Post-synthesis / post-implementation (functional and timing) simulation
tools.description: Simulate the netlist produced by synthesis or implementation instead of the RTL: -mode post-synthesis or post-implementation with -type functional (gate-level netlist, UNISIM models, no delays) or -type timing (netlist plus SDF back-annotation, including routing delays after implementation, which also models reset/GSR timing and clock skew). Timing simulation is the only way to catch functional issues that depend on real delays (e.g. unconstrained paths, missed multicycle constraints) and to verify I/O timing when the interface cannot be constrained fully. Project Mode does the write_verilog/write_sdf and library setup automatically.
tools.usage:
launch_simulation -mode post-synthesis|post-implementation -type functional|timing [-simset <simset>] [-scripts_only] [-noclean_dir] [-absolute_path] [-install_path <dir>]
# non-project equivalent
open_checkpoint post_route.dcp
write_verilog -mode timesim -sdf_anno true -sdf_file top_time.sdf -force top_time.v
write_sdf -mode timesim -force top_time.sdf
xvlog -sv top_time.v tb.sv ; xelab -L simprims_ver -L secureip glbl work.tb -s tb_time -sdfmax /tb/dut=top_time.sdf ; xsim tb_time -R

parameters.name: -mode
parameters.description: behavioral (RTL), post-synthesis, post-implementation.

parameters.name: -type
parameters.description: functional (no delays) or timing (SDF annotated; post-implementation only for accurate routing delays).

parameters.name: -scripts_only
parameters.description: Generate the compile/elaborate/run scripts without launching, for CI.

parameters.name: glbl
parameters.description: Verilog netlists need the glbl module (GSR/GTS) elaborated alongside the testbench; VHDL netlists use the simprim/unisim libraries.

tools.example:
# Project mode: Flow Navigator > Run Simulation > Run Post-Implementation Timing Simulation
launch_simulation -mode post-implementation -type timing
run 20 us
# The testbench must wait for GSR release (~100 ns) before applying stimulus in timing simulation.
tools.notes: Netlist simulation of encrypted IP needs the secureip library and the IP's simulation output products. Timing simulation is slow and uses the worst-case (max) delays by default; check the xelab -sdfmax/-sdfmin selection. VHDL post-implementation timing simulation is not supported for all families (use the Verilog netlist with a VHDL testbench via mixed language).

tools.name: xelab DPI-C options (-sv_lib, -sv_root, -dpiheader) and compile_c / xsc
tools.description: SystemVerilog DPI-C support in xsim: C/C++ functions imported into SV are compiled to a shared library with xsc (the xsim C compiler wrapper around gcc/clang, or compile_c from Tcl), xelab -dpiheader generates the C header for exported/imported functions, and -sv_lib <lib> / -sv_root <dir> tell xelab which shared library (without extension) to load at run time. Used for C reference models, file I/O helpers, and co-simulation with host software.
tools.usage:
xsc -c dpi_model.c -o dpi_model.o ; xsc --shared dpi_model.o -o dpi.so   (dpi.dll on Windows)
xelab -dpiheader dpi.h work.tb              ;# generate header from SV import/export
xelab -L uvm -sv_root . -sv_lib dpi -debug typical work.tb -s tb_sim
xsim tb_sim -R
# Project mode: set_property -name {xsim.elaborate.xelab.more_options} -value {-sv_lib dpi -sv_root ./dpi} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]

parameters.name: -sv_lib <name>
parameters.description: Shared library name without extension; repeatable.

parameters.name: -sv_root <dir>
parameters.description: Directory searched for the library (default current dir).

parameters.name: -dpiheader <file>
parameters.description: Write a C header with prototypes for the DPI functions found in the design.

parameters.name: -dpi_absolute
parameters.description: Treat -sv_root as absolute path.

parameters.name: xsc options
parameters.description: -c compile only, --shared link shared library, -i/--gcc_compile_options, --additional_option, -work, -v verbose.

tools.notes: The GCC bundled with Vivado (tps/gcc) is used unless --gcc_compile_options points elsewhere; mixing a different compiler version can break the run-time load. In Project Mode add the C files to sim_1 and set the xsim.elaborate.xelab.more_options property; Vivado runs xsc automatically for .c/.cpp sources in the simulation fileset.

tools.name: xelab timing-simulation options (-sdfmax, -sdfmin, -sdfroot, -transport_int_delays, -pulse_r/-pulse_e, -notimingchecks)
tools.description: Options that control SDF back-annotation and delay modelling when elaborating a timing netlist: -sdfmax/-sdfmin (or -sdftyp) attach an SDF file to an instance path with the max/min delay set, -sdfroot changes the root instance the SDF paths are relative to, -transport_int_delays selects transport instead of inertial delay on interconnect, -pulse_r/-pulse_e set the reject/error pulse limits as a percentage of the path delay, -pulse_int_r/-pulse_int_e do the same for interconnect, and -notimingchecks or -timescale/-override_timeunit adjust checks and time units. These map to the xsim.elaborate.* properties in Project Mode.
tools.usage:
xelab -L simprims_ver -L secureip -L unisims_ver glbl work.tb -s tb_time \
  -sdfmax /tb/dut=./top_time.sdf -transport_int_delays -pulse_r 0 -pulse_int_r 0 -pulse_e 0 -pulse_int_e 0 \
  -debug typical --timescale 1ps/1ps

parameters.name: -sdfmax / -sdfmin <instance>=<file.sdf>
parameters.description: Annotate max (setup-critical) or min (hold-critical) delays onto the named instance.

parameters.name: -sdfroot <instance>
parameters.description: Root instance for the SDF (when the SDF was written for a sub-hierarchy).

parameters.name: -transport_int_delays
parameters.description: Interconnect delays use transport model (pulses pass); default inertial model swallows narrow pulses.

parameters.name: -pulse_r / -pulse_e / -pulse_int_r / -pulse_int_e <0-100>
parameters.description: Pulse reject and error thresholds in percent of the delay for gates and interconnect.

parameters.name: -notimingchecks
parameters.description: Disable setup/hold/recovery checks (debug only).

parameters.name: --timescale / -override_timeunit / -override_timeprecision
parameters.description: Default and forced time units.

tools.example:
# Project mode equivalents (Settings > Simulation > Elaboration)
set_property -name {xsim.elaborate.xelab.more_options} -value {-transport_int_delays -pulse_r 0 -pulse_e 0} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.elaborate.sdf_delay} -value {sdfmin} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
tools.notes: Vivado's default launch_simulation timing settings use max delays, transport interconnect delays and zero pulse thresholds, which matches the recommended sign-off setup in UG900. Setup/hold violations print as $setuphold messages from the SIMPRIM models.

tools.name: xsim run-time options (-tclbatch, -wdb, -view, -gui, -R, -onfinish, -log, -testplusarg)
tools.description: Command-line switches of the xsim executable when running a snapshot: -R runs to completion and exits, -gui opens the waveform GUI, -tclbatch <file> runs a Tcl script (typically open_vcd/log_wave/run all) in batch, -wdb names the waveform database to write, -view <wcfg> loads a waveform configuration in the GUI, -onfinish quit|stop controls behaviour at $finish, -onerror quit|stop at errors, -log names the log, -testplusarg name=value passes $test$plusargs/$value$plusargs to the testbench, -sv_seed sets the randomisation seed and -maxdeltaid limits delta cycles to catch zero-delay loops.
tools.usage: xsim <snapshot> [-R] [-gui] [-tclbatch <script.tcl>] [-t <script.tcl>] [-wdb <file.wdb>] [-view <file.wcfg>] [-onfinish quit|stop] [-onerror quit|stop] [-log <file>] [-testplusarg <name=value>] [-sv_seed <n>] [-maxdeltaid <n>] [-ieeewarnings] [-nolog] [-stats] [-protoinst <file>] [-vcdfile <file>] [-vcdunit <unit>]

parameters.name: -R
parameters.description: Run all and quit (batch regression).

parameters.name: -tclbatch / -t
parameters.description: Execute the Tcl file after loading the snapshot; must end with quit for batch runs.

parameters.name: -wdb
parameters.description: Waveform database file (needs log_wave or add_wave in the script).

parameters.name: -view
parameters.description: Waveform configuration(s) to open with -gui.

parameters.name: -testplusarg
parameters.description: Plusargs for $test$plusargs; repeatable.

parameters.name: -sv_seed
parameters.description: Seed for SystemVerilog randomize().

tools.example:
# run.tcl
open_vcd dump.vcd
log_vcd /tb/dut/*
log_wave -recursive *
run all
close_vcd
quit
$ xsim tb_sim -tclbatch run.tcl -wdb tb_sim.wdb -testplusarg TESTNAME=smoke -sv_seed 42 -onerror quit
$ xsim tb_sim -gui -view tb_sim.wcfg   # inspect later
tools.notes: -gui with a script: use -t so the script runs before handing over the GUI. Exit codes: non-zero on errors when -onerror quit is used, useful for CI. Vivado's launch_simulation generates <sim>/xsim/*.sh/.bat wrappers that call exactly these commands.

tools.name: xelab -L library search, -relax, -mt, -O and the .prj project file (-prj)
tools.description: Elaboration setup options: -L <lib> adds a compiled library to the search order (unisims_ver, unimacro_ver, simprims_ver, secureip, xpm, uvm, plus IP libraries such as axi_vip_v1_1_x and fifo_generator_v13_2_x whose names appear in the IP's simulation scripts), -relax loosens strict LRM checking for legacy code, -mt on|off|<n> controls multithreaded compilation, -O0..3 sets optimisation (-O3 fastest run, -O0 best debug), -debug typical|all|wave|line|off decides what is visible in the waveform/probes, and -prj <file.prj> compiles a list of sources given in a project file (one 'verilog|sv|vhdl|vhdl2008 <lib> <files...>' line each) instead of separate xvlog/xvhdl runs. -a produces a standalone executable, -R runs immediately after elaboration.
tools.usage:
xelab -prj tb.prj -L unisims_ver -L secureip -L xpm -debug typical -relax -mt 8 -O2 --timescale 1ns/1ps work.tb work.glbl -s tb_sim
# tb.prj
sv     work ./tb/tb_top.sv ./tb/pkg.sv
verilog work ./rtl/top.v
vhdl2008 mylib ./rtl/pkg.vhd ./rtl/core.vhd
# library locations from compile_simlib / IP output: xsim.ini (project) or $XILINX_VIVADO/data/xsim/xsim.ini (defaults)

parameters.name: -L <library>
parameters.description: Add a library to the reference search; repeatable. Library paths are resolved via xsim.ini.

parameters.name: -prj <file>
parameters.description: Project file listing sources with language and library.

parameters.name: -debug
parameters.description: off (fastest), typical (signals visible), wave (waveform only), line (line stepping), all.

parameters.name: -relax
parameters.description: Relaxed rule checking (common for vendor netlists and old code).

parameters.name: -mt
parameters.description: Multi-threading: auto/off/N.

parameters.name: -generic_top / -generic
parameters.description: Override top-level generics/parameters, e.g. -generic_top "WIDTH=16".

parameters.name: -d <macro> / -i <dir>
parameters.description: Verilog defines and include directories (elaboration-time for -prj compiles).

parameters.name: -initfile / -include
parameters.description: Memory initialisation and include paths.

tools.notes: Library names include the IP version, so scripts break across Vivado releases; use export_simulation or launch_simulation -scripts_only to regenerate them. xsim.ini maps logical library names to directories; a project's xsim.ini is written into <project>.sim/sim_1/behav/xsim.

tools.name: add_wave_divider / add_wave_group / add_wave_marker / add_wave_virtual_bus
tools.description: Organise the waveform window from Tcl: add_wave_divider inserts a labelled separator, add_wave_group creates a collapsible group (into which add_wave -into places signals), add_wave_marker adds a named time marker (cursor) at a time, and add_wave_virtual_bus combines several signals into one bus for display (with -radix). Together with add_wave and save_wave_config they let a script build a reusable, documented waveform layout for a testbench.
tools.usage:
add_wave_divider [-into <group>] [-at_wave <wave>] [-after_wave <wave>] [-before_wave <wave>] [-color <c>] [<name>]
add_wave_group [-into <group>] [-at_wave|-after_wave|-before_wave <wave>] [-color <c>] [<name>]
add_wave_marker [-into <group>] [-name <n>] [-color <c>] [-quiet] <time> [<unit>]
add_wave_virtual_bus [-into <group>] [-radix <r>] [-color <c>] [-reverse] [-quiet] <name> <hdl_objects>

parameters.name: -into
parameters.description: Group (from add_wave_group) or wave configuration to place the item in.

parameters.name: -at_wave / -after_wave / -before_wave
parameters.description: Position relative to an existing wave object.

parameters.name: -radix
parameters.description: bin, hex, unsigned, signed, ascii, oct, dec for virtual buses.

parameters.name: -reverse
parameters.description: Reverse the bit order of the virtual bus.

tools.example:
set g_axi [add_wave_group "AXI write"]
add_wave_divider -into $g_axi "address channel"
add_wave -into $g_axi -radix hex /tb/dut/s_axi_awaddr /tb/dut/s_axi_awvalid /tb/dut/s_axi_awready
add_wave_divider -into $g_axi "data channel"
add_wave -into $g_axi -radix hex /tb/dut/s_axi_wdata /tb/dut/s_axi_wvalid
add_wave_virtual_bus -radix hex ctrl_bus {/tb/dut/en /tb/dut/mode[1:0] /tb/dut/rst}
add_wave_marker -name "first write" 1250 ns
save_wave_config ./tb_axi.wcfg
tools.notes: Wave objects returned by these commands can be reused as -into targets. In batch mode (no GUI) the commands still work and the layout is saved in the .wcfg for later viewing with xsim -gui -view.

tools.name: save_wave_config / open_wave_config / close_wave_config / current_wave_config / get_wave_configs
tools.description: Manage waveform configuration files (.wcfg): save_wave_config writes the current window layout (signals, groups, dividers, radixes, markers, zoom), open_wave_config loads one (or creates an empty configuration with create_wave_config), close_wave_config closes it and current_wave_config selects among several open configurations. Vivado adds a saved .wcfg to the simulation fileset so it opens automatically on the next launch_simulation.
tools.usage:
save_wave_config [-object <wcfg>] [-quiet] [<filename.wcfg>]
open_wave_config [-quiet] [<filename.wcfg>]
create_wave_config [-quiet] [<name>]
close_wave_config [-force] [-quiet] [<wcfg>]
current_wave_config [<wcfg>]
get_wave_configs [-regexp] [-nocase] [-filter <expr>] [<patterns>]

parameters.name: <filename.wcfg>
parameters.description: Path; relative paths resolve from the simulation run directory.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Close without prompting to save.

tools.example:
open_wave_config ./tb_axi.wcfg
run 5 us
save_wave_config
# multiple layouts
create_wave_config debug_fifo
add_wave /tb/dut/u_fifo/*
save_wave_config ./fifo.wcfg
# project mode: the .wcfg is added with add_files -fileset sim_1 ./tb_axi.wcfg
tools.notes: A .wcfg references signals by hierarchical name; renamed instances break entries (they show as missing objects). log_wave is required for signals to have data in a reopened .wdb.

tools.name: remove_forces
tools.description: Release forces applied with add_force on signals or on all forced objects, returning control to the design drivers (a force that was -cancel_after will expire by itself). It is used in testbench scripts that inject faults or temporarily override inputs and need to restore normal operation.
tools.usage: remove_forces [-quiet] [-all] [<force_ids_or_objects>]

parameters.name: -all
parameters.description: Remove every active force.

parameters.name: <force_ids>
parameters.description: Force objects returned by add_force, or the HDL objects being forced.

tools.example:
set f [add_force /tb/dut/link_up 0]
run 500 ns
remove_forces $f
# or
add_force /tb/dut/rst {1 0ns} {0 100ns} -repeat_every 1us
run 3 us
remove_forces -all
tools.notes: Forced values ride over any driver, including clocks; forcing a clock net to a constant stops the design.

tools.name: add_bp / remove_bps / report_bps
tools.description: Source-level breakpoints for HDL debugging: add_bp sets a breakpoint at a file and line (the snapshot must be elaborated with -debug typical/all/line), run/step then stop when execution reaches it, report_bps lists active breakpoints and remove_bps deletes them. Combined with step, current_frame, get_value and report_values this gives a debugger-like flow for procedural code and testbenches.
tools.usage:
add_bp [-quiet] <file_name> <line_number>
remove_bps [-all] [-file <file> -line <n>] [-quiet] [<bp_ids>]
report_bps [-quiet] [<bp_ids>]

parameters.name: <file_name> <line_number>
parameters.description: Source file (as compiled) and line.

parameters.name: -all
parameters.description: Remove every breakpoint.

tools.example:
add_bp ./tb/tb_top.sv 142
run all              ;# stops at line 142
get_value /tb_top/expected
step                 ;# execute one statement
report_bps
remove_bps -all
run all
tools.notes: Breakpoints in always blocks trigger on every activation; use conditional logic in the testbench or add_condition for value-based stops. In Project Mode, breakpoints can also be set by clicking the gutter in the source editor while the simulation is running.

tools.name: add_condition / remove_conditions / report_conditions
tools.description: Conditional actions during simulation: add_condition evaluates an HDL boolean expression at every change of its operands and, when it becomes true, runs a Tcl command (e.g. stop, puts, get_value, report_values). It is xsim's equivalent of a watchpoint or a scripted assertion, and is used to stop the simulation on an error flag, dump state when a rare event happens, or count occurrences.
tools.usage:
add_condition [-name <name>] [-radix <r>] [-notrace] [-quiet] <condition_expression> <tcl_command>
remove_conditions [-all] [<condition_ids>]
report_conditions [<condition_ids>]

parameters.name: <condition_expression>
parameters.description: HDL object comparison such as {/tb/dut/err_flag == 1} or {/tb/dut/state == 3'b101}.

parameters.name: <tcl_command>
parameters.description: Tcl to run; braces allow multi-line scripts.

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Name for reporting/removal.

tools.notes: Conditions are checked in the simulation kernel; many complex conditions slow the run. Objects must be logged/visible (-debug typical) for the expression to bind.

tools.name: step / current_frame / report_frames
tools.description: Single-step execution and call-stack inspection: step runs one HDL statement (entering procedures/functions), current_frame selects a stack frame of the current process for value inspection, and report_frames prints the call stack when simulation is stopped at a breakpoint inside nested tasks or functions. They require -debug typical or all (line stepping needs -debug line/all).
tools.usage:
step [-quiet]
current_frame [-set] [-up] [-down] [-quiet] [<frame_index>]
report_frames [-quiet]

parameters.name: -up / -down
parameters.description: Move one frame towards the caller / callee.

parameters.name: <frame_index>
parameters.description: Absolute frame number from report_frames.

tools.example:
add_bp ./tb/checker.sv 57
run all
report_frames
current_frame -up
get_value expected_word
step ; step
current_scope
tools.notes: Stepping through concurrent processes shows one process at a time; the Tcl console prints the file:line reached; step alone advances by one statement.

tools.name: current_time
tools.description: Return the current simulation time of the running xsim session as a string with units (e.g. 1250 ns), used in scripts for logging, computing run lengths relative to now, and assertions on when events happen.
tools.usage: current_time [-quiet]
tools.example:
run 1 us
puts "now: [current_time]"
set t0 [current_time]
run all
# typical: run until a condition then record the time
add_condition {/tb/done == 1} {puts "done at [current_time]"; stop}
tools.notes: The value is formatted in the simulation's time unit; parse with scan or regexp when arithmetic is needed. Use run <n> <unit> for relative advances rather than absolute times.

tools.name: report_values / get_objects / get_scopes / report_scopes / report_objects
tools.description: Inspect the design hierarchy and values in an xsim session: get_scopes returns scope (instance/block/process) objects under the current scope, get_objects returns HDL objects (signals, variables, constants, ports) matching a pattern with -filter on type/properties, report_values prints the current value of objects (with -radix), and report_scopes / report_objects print listings. They are the scripted counterpart of the Scope and Objects windows and are used to dump state, verify values in regression scripts and build waveform lists dynamically.
tools.usage:
get_scopes [-r|-recursive] [-regexp] [-nocase] [-filter <expr>] [-quiet] [<patterns>]
get_objects [-r|-recursive] [-regexp] [-nocase] [-filter <expr>] [-local] [-quiet] [<patterns>]
report_values [-radix <r>] [-quiet] [<hdl_objects>]
report_scopes [-quiet] [<scopes>]
report_objects [-quiet] [<objects>]

parameters.name: -recursive
parameters.description: Descend into sub-scopes.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: e.g. {type == signal}, {type == port && direction == in}, {name =~ *valid*}.

parameters.name: -radix
parameters.description: Display radix for report_values (bin, hex, unsigned, dec, ascii, ...).

tools.example:
current_scope /tb/dut
report_values -radix hex [get_objects -filter {type == port} *]
foreach s [get_scopes -r -filter {type == module}] { puts $s }
add_wave [get_objects -r -filter {name =~ *axis_tvalid*} /tb/dut/*]
puts [get_value -radix unsigned /tb/dut/cnt]
tools.notes: get_value returns a single value; report_values prints a table. Object types: signal, variable, constant, port, parameter, generic, event, process. Large -r queries on big designs are slow; scope first with current_scope.

tools.name: describe
tools.description: Print the declaration details of an HDL object or scope in the simulation: type, width, range, direction, the source file and line where it is declared, and for scopes the module/entity and its parameters. Used interactively to check a signal's declared width or a parameter's resolved value without opening the source.
tools.usage: describe [-quiet] <hdl_objects_or_scopes>

parameters.name: <hdl_objects_or_scopes>
parameters.description: Hierarchical names or objects from get_objects/get_scopes.

tools.example:
describe /tb/dut/rx_data
describe /tb/dut/u_fifo
describe [get_objects -filter {type == parameter} /tb/dut/*]
tools.notes: Equivalent to hovering in the Objects window. For parameters the value shown is the elaborated one, including -generic_top overrides.

tools.name: open_wave_database / close_sim / relaunch_sim / current_sim
tools.description: Session management: open_wave_database opens a previously written .wdb file in the waveform viewer (static, no further running) for post-mortem analysis of a batch run, close_sim ends the running simulation and releases the snapshot, relaunch_sim recompiles changed sources and restarts the simulation in Project Mode keeping the waveform layout, and current_sim returns/selects the active simulation when several are open.
tools.usage:
open_wave_database [-quiet] <file.wdb>
close_sim [-force] [-quiet]
relaunch_sim [-quiet]
current_sim [-quiet] [<sim>]

parameters.name: <file.wdb>
parameters.description: Waveform database written by xsim -wdb or launch_simulation (default <top>_behav.wdb).

parameters.name: -force (close_sim)
parameters.description: Close without prompting about unsaved wave configurations.

tools.example:
# after a batch run: xsim tb_sim -tclbatch run.tcl -wdb regress.wdb
open_wave_database ./regress.wdb
open_wave_config ./tb_axi.wcfg
# project mode edit-compile-debug loop
relaunch_sim
run 10 us
close_sim -force
tools.notes: A .wdb only contains signals that were logged (log_wave); log_wave -r / everything for post-mortem debugging but expect large files. relaunch_sim is what the GUI 'Relaunch Simulation' button runs.

tools.name: ltrace / ptrace
tools.description: Execution tracing in xsim: ltrace on prints each HDL source line as it executes (line trace) and ptrace on prints process activations (process trace), both to the console/log; off disables them. They are heavy but useful to understand why a process runs (sensitivity list surprises), to catch zero-delay oscillation, or to see the order of concurrent statements at a time step.
tools.usage:
ltrace on|off [-quiet]
ptrace on|off [-quiet]

parameters.name: on / off
parameters.description: Enable or disable tracing from the current time.

tools.example:
run 990 ns
ltrace on
ptrace on
run 20 ns        ;# every executed line and activated process is printed
ltrace off
ptrace off
tools.notes: Requires -debug all or line for line tracing. Combine with -maxdeltaid on xsim to detect infinite delta cycles.

tools.name: config_wave
tools.description: Set waveform-window options for the current wave configuration from Tcl: default radix, signal name display (short/long), zoom/time-unit settings, and whether to display in time or delta-cycle mode. It replaces the GUI's Waveform Options for scripted setups.
tools.usage: config_wave [-default_radix <radix>] [-signal_name_width <n>] [-name_display short|long] [-quiet]

parameters.name: -default_radix
parameters.description: Radix for objects added without -radix: bin, hex, dec, unsigned, signed, oct, ascii, sfix/ufix.

parameters.name: -signal_name_width
parameters.description: Number of name levels shown (0 = full path).

tools.example:
config_wave -default_radix hex -signal_name_width 1
add_wave /tb/dut/*
tools.notes: Run config_wave -help in a session for the exact option set of your release; the same settings are stored in the .wcfg.

tools.name: open_saif / log_saif / close_saif (SAIF for power analysis)
tools.description: Record switching activity during an xsim run into a SAIF file for report_power: open_saif creates the file, log_saif selects the objects (usually the DUT's internal nets recursively, on a post-synthesis or post-implementation netlist so names match), the run accumulates toggle counts and close_saif writes the file. Vivado's read_saif then annotates the design; the xsim.simulate.saif* properties automate this in Project Mode.
tools.usage:
open_saif <file.saif>
log_saif [-quiet] <hdl_objects>
run <time>
close_saif
# project mode
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.saif} -value {power.saif} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.saif_scope} -value {/tb_top/dut} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.saif_all_signals} -value {true} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]

parameters.name: log_saif <objects>
parameters.description: Typically [get_objects -r /tb/dut/*] to include every net below the DUT.

parameters.name: xsim.simulate.saif_scope
parameters.description: Instance whose activity is logged; used with read_saif -strip_path.

tools.example:
# run.tcl for a post-implementation functional simulation
open_saif ./post_impl.saif
log_saif [get_objects -r /tb_top/dut/*]
run 200 us
close_saif
quit
# then in Vivado
open_checkpoint post_route.dcp
read_saif -strip_path tb_top/dut ./post_impl.saif
report_power -file power_saif.rpt
tools.notes: Log only after reset/initialisation and over a representative window; the SAIF averages activity over the logged interval. RTL-level SAIF names rarely match the implemented netlist, so post-synthesis or later is recommended.

tools.name: open_vcd / log_vcd / close_vcd / flush_vcd / limit_vcd (VCD output)
tools.description: Write a Value Change Dump from xsim: open_vcd creates the file (or the default dump.vcd), log_vcd chooses the objects (with -level for hierarchy depth), the run records changes, flush_vcd forces buffered data out, limit_vcd caps the file size and close_vcd finalises it. Also reachable through $dumpfile/$dumpvars in Verilog testbenches. Used to hand waveforms to third-party viewers (GTKWave), to compare against other simulators or to feed VCD-based power tools.
tools.usage:
open_vcd [<file.vcd>]
log_vcd [-level <n>] [-quiet] [<hdl_objects>]
flush_vcd
limit_vcd <size_bytes>
close_vcd [-quiet]
current_vcd [<vcd>]
checkpoint_vcd

parameters.name: -level
parameters.description: Hierarchy levels below the objects to include (0 = all).

parameters.name: limit_vcd <size>
parameters.description: Stop dumping once the file exceeds the size.

tools.example:
open_vcd ./waves.vcd
log_vcd -level 0 /tb/dut
run 50 us
close_vcd
# Verilog alternative in the testbench
initial begin $dumpfile("waves.vcd"); $dumpvars(0, tb); end
tools.notes: VCD files grow quickly; prefer the native .wdb (log_wave) for xsim-only debugging. Multi-dimensional arrays and some SystemVerilog types are not dumped to VCD.

tools.name: report_drivers
tools.description: List the drivers of a signal in the current simulation: every process/statement (with file and line) and continuous assignment that drives it, with the value each contributes, which resolves X and multiple-driver problems and shows why a net has an unexpected value.
tools.usage: report_drivers [-quiet] <hdl_objects>

parameters.name: <hdl_objects>
parameters.description: Signals or nets to analyse.

tools.example:
run 2 us
report_drivers /tb/dut/shared_bus
# shows e.g. two OBUFT-like drivers with conflicting values -> X
tools.notes: Equivalent to right-click > Report Drivers in the Objects/Waveform windows.

tools.name: Simulation settings properties (xsim.compile.*, xsim.elaborate.*, xsim.simulate.*)
tools.description: Project Mode stores every option of the three xsim phases as properties on the simulation fileset, editable in Settings > Simulation or with set_property -name ... -objects [get_filesets sim_1]. Compile: xsim.compile.xvlog.more_options, xsim.compile.xvhdl.more_options, xsim.compile.xvlog.relax, xsim.compile.xvlog.nosort, xsim.compile.tcl.pre; elaborate: xsim.elaborate.xelab.more_options, xsim.elaborate.debug_level (typical/all/off), xsim.elaborate.relax, xsim.elaborate.mt_level, xsim.elaborate.load_glbl, xsim.elaborate.sdf_delay (sdfmin/sdfmax), xsim.elaborate.rangecheck, xsim.elaborate.snapshot; simulate: xsim.simulate.runtime, xsim.simulate.log_all_signals, xsim.simulate.wdb, xsim.simulate.custom_tcl, xsim.simulate.tcl.post, xsim.simulate.saif/saif_scope/saif_all_signals, xsim.simulate.xsim.more_options. Equivalent families exist for other simulators (modelsim.*, questa.*, vcs.*, xcelium.*, riviera.*).
tools.usage:
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.runtime} -value {100us} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.log_all_signals} -value {true} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.elaborate.debug_level} -value {all} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.compile.xvlog.more_options} -value {-d SIM_FAST=1 -i ./include} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.elaborate.xelab.more_options} -value {-sv_lib dpi -sv_root ./dpi -O2} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.custom_tcl} -value {./run_regress.tcl} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
report_property [get_filesets sim_1] xsim.*

parameters.name: xsim.simulate.runtime
parameters.description: Time to run after launch (e.g. 1000ns, all for run all).

parameters.name: xsim.simulate.log_all_signals
parameters.description: log_wave -r on everything so any signal can be added to the wave later.

parameters.name: xsim.elaborate.debug_level
parameters.description: typical (default), all, off (fastest).

parameters.name: xsim.simulate.custom_tcl / xsim.simulate.tcl.post
parameters.description: Tcl scripts run instead of / after the default run.

parameters.name: xsim.elaborate.load_glbl
parameters.description: Include glbl for Verilog netlist/IP simulation (default true).

parameters.name: *.more_options
parameters.description: Pass-through strings appended to xvlog/xvhdl/xelab/xsim command lines.

tools.example:
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.runtime} -value {all} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.saif} -value {activity.saif} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
launch_simulation -mode post-implementation -type functional
tools.notes: Property names are release-dependent (list them with report_property [get_filesets sim_1] xsim.*). Every launch regenerates <project>.sim/sim_1/<mode>/xsim/ scripts from these settings; launch_simulation -scripts_only writes them without running.

tools.name: Simulation fileset: sim_1, simulation top, generics, defines, include dirs (create_fileset -simset, set_property top/generic/verilog_define/include_dirs)
tools.description: Simulation sources live in simulation filesets (sim_1 by default; more with create_fileset -simset for different testbenches) which inherit the design sources and add testbench files, .wcfg, .mem/.dat data and C DPI sources. The fileset's top property names the testbench top, generic passes top-level generics/parameters (-generic_top), verilog_define and include_dirs set macros and include paths for compilation (also settable on sources_1 for synthesis), and current_fileset -simset / launch_simulation -simset choose which set runs. Files can be marked simulation-only with USED_IN or by living only in the sim fileset.
tools.usage:
create_fileset -simset sim_axi
add_files -fileset sim_axi -norecurse {./tb/tb_axi.sv ./tb/axi_pkg.sv ./tb/stimulus.mem}
set_property top tb_axi [get_filesets sim_axi]
set_property top_lib xil_defaultlib [get_filesets sim_axi]
set_property generic {WIDTH=16 USE_FAST=1} [get_filesets sim_axi]
set_property verilog_define {SIMULATION=1 SEED=7} [get_filesets sim_axi]
set_property include_dirs [list ./tb/include ./rtl/include] [get_filesets sim_axi]
set_property -name {xsim.simulate.runtime} -value {all} -objects [get_filesets sim_axi]
current_fileset -simset [get_filesets sim_axi]
launch_simulation -simset sim_axi

parameters.name: top / top_lib
parameters.description: Testbench top module/entity and its library.

parameters.name: generic
parameters.description: List of NAME=VALUE generics/parameters for the top.

parameters.name: verilog_define
parameters.description: List of NAME or NAME=VALUE macros passed as xvlog -d.

parameters.name: include_dirs
parameters.description: Directories for `include; files can also be marked IS_GLOBAL_INCLUDE for automatic inclusion.

parameters.name: source_set
parameters.description: Design fileset the simset builds on (default sources_1).

tools.example:
# Global include header and a simulation-only file
set_property IS_GLOBAL_INCLUDE true [get_files ./rtl/include/defines.vh]
set_property USED_IN {simulation} [get_files ./tb/sim_models.sv]
update_compile_order -fileset sim_1
report_compile_order -fileset sim_1
tools.notes: A testbench file placed in sources_1 will be synthesized (or error) unless USED_IN excludes synthesis. Generics on the fileset apply only to simulation; synthesis generics are set with synth_design -generic or the run's STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.MORE OPTIONS.

tools.name: Third-party simulators: set_property target_simulator (ModelSim/Questa, VCS, Xcelium, Riviera-PRO) and compiled-library settings
tools.description: Vivado can drive Siemens ModelSim/Questa, Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium (and legacy IES) and Aldec Riviera-PRO/Active-HDL instead of xsim: set target_simulator on the project, point compxlib.modelsim_compiled_library_dir (or the questa/vcs/xcelium/riviera variants) at the libraries produced by compile_simlib, optionally set the simulator's install path, and launch_simulation then generates that simulator's compile/elaborate/run scripts (vlog/vcom/vsim, vlogan/vhdlan/vcs, xmvlog/xmvhdl/xmelab/xmsim, vlog/vcom/vsim for Riviera) and starts it. Per-simulator properties mirror the xsim.* ones (modelsim.simulate.runtime, questa.compile.vlog.more_options, vcs.elaborate.vcs.more_options, xcelium.simulate.xmsim.more_options ...). Version support is listed in the release notes (UG973).
tools.usage:
set_property target_simulator Questa [current_project]      ;# XSim, ModelSim, Questa, VCS, Xcelium, Riviera, ActiveHDL
set_property compxlib.questa_compiled_library_dir /tools/simlibs/questa_2024.3 [current_project]
set_property -name {questa.simulate.runtime} -value {all} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
set_property -name {questa.compile.vlog.more_options} -value {-suppress 2892} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]
launch_simulation -simset sim_1
# script-only for CI / other hosts
export_simulation -simulator questa -lib_map_path /tools/simlibs/questa_2024.3 -directory ./export_sim -of_objects [get_filesets sim_1]

parameters.name: target_simulator
parameters.description: Project property choosing the simulator.

parameters.name: compxlib.<sim>_compiled_library_dir
parameters.description: Location of the unisim/simprim/secureip/xpm and IP libraries compiled with compile_simlib for that simulator version.

parameters.name: <sim>.simulate.runtime / <sim>.compile.*.more_options / <sim>.elaborate.*.more_options
parameters.description: Per-phase options for each simulator.

parameters.name: Tools > Settings > Simulation > Simulator
parameters.description: GUI location; also the 'Simulator executable path' field (simulator install).

tools.example:
compile_simlib -simulator questa -simulator_exec_path /tools/questa/bin -family all -language all -library all -directory /tools/simlibs/questa_2024.3
set_property target_simulator Questa [current_project]
set_property compxlib.questa_compiled_library_dir /tools/simlibs/questa_2024.3 [current_project]
launch_simulation
tools.notes: Encrypted IP requires the secureip library compiled for the exact simulator version supported by the Vivado release. modelsim.ini / cds.lib / synopsys_sim.setup files are generated in the simulation run directory; export_simulation packages everything for a machine without Vivado.

tools.name: SystemVerilog and UVM support in xsim
tools.description: xsim supports SystemVerilog for both design and verification: classes, interfaces with modports, packages, constrained randomisation (randomize with, rand/randc, constraints), covergroups and coverpoints (functional coverage with xcrg reporting), immediate and concurrent assertions (SVA, including sequences and properties in checkers), DPI-C, clocking blocks, program blocks, and the precompiled UVM 1.2 library (xelab -L uvm, `include "uvm_macros.svh"`, import uvm_pkg::*) with run_test and +UVM_TESTNAME via -testplusarg. It is sufficient for typical IP-level UVM environments; the AXI VIP and other AMD VIP are built on it.
tools.usage:
xvlog -sv -L uvm tb_pkg.sv tb_top.sv
xelab -L uvm -debug typical -timescale 1ns/1ps work.tb_top -s uvm_sim
xsim uvm_sim -testplusarg UVM_TESTNAME=axi_smoke_test -testplusarg UVM_VERBOSITY=UVM_MEDIUM -R
# project mode: set_property -name {xsim.elaborate.xelab.more_options} -value {-L uvm} ...; add -L uvm to xvlog via xsim.compile.xvlog.more_options

parameters.name: -L uvm
parameters.description: Use the precompiled UVM library shipped in <install>/data/system_verilog/uvm_1.2.

parameters.name: -testplusarg UVM_TESTNAME=<test>
parameters.description: Select the UVM test at run time.

parameters.name: xelab -cc_type / xcrg
parameters.description: Code (line/branch/condition/toggle) and functional coverage collection and reporting (2022.2 and later).

parameters.name: -sv_seed
parameters.description: Randomisation seed.

tools.notes: Unsupported or limited constructs are listed per release in UG900's SystemVerilog chapter (e.g. some dynamic-array constraint forms, checker instantiation limits). Performance is lower than commercial simulators for large UVM benches; export_simulation to Questa/VCS/Xcelium for regressions.

tools.name: Code coverage in xsim (xelab -cc_type / -cc_db, xcrg)
tools.description: Code and functional coverage support added to xsim in the 2022.2 timeframe: enable collection at elaboration with -cc_type selecting line (l), branch (b), condition (c), toggle (t) and statement (s) coverage, name the coverage database with -cc_db and directory with -cc_dir, run the simulation to accumulate data, then merge and report databases with the xcrg utility (HTML or text report). Functional coverage from covergroups is stored alongside.
tools.usage:
xelab -cc_type lbct -cc_db cov_run1 -cc_dir ./coverage -debug typical work.tb -s tb_cov
xsim tb_cov -R
xcrg -report_format html -dir ./coverage -report_dir ./coverage/html
xcrg -merge_dir ./coverage -merge_db_name merged -dir ./coverage_run1 ./coverage_run2
# project mode
set_property -name {xsim.elaborate.xelab.more_options} -value {-cc_type lbct -cc_db cov} -objects [get_filesets sim_1]

parameters.name: -cc_type <letters>
parameters.description: Any combination of l (line), b (branch), c (condition), t (toggle), s (statement).

parameters.name: -cc_db <name> / -cc_dir <dir>
parameters.description: Coverage database name and location.

parameters.name: xcrg -report_format html|text
parameters.description: Report generator; -merge_dir/-merge_db_name merge several runs (see xcrg -help for exclusion options).

tools.notes: Feature details and option names evolve between releases (check xelab -help and xcrg -help); the Vivado GUI has no coverage viewer, the HTML report is the primary view. export_xsim_coverage is the Tcl-side helper in recent releases.

tools.name: Protected (encrypted) IP and secureip simulation
tools.description: Encrypted simulation models are used for hard blocks (transceivers, PCIe, MMCM/PLL behavioural details, DDR PHYs) and for licensed IP: the models are IEEE 1735 encrypted and shipped precompiled for xsim (secureip library) and compiled by compile_simlib for third-party simulators, so they simulate but cannot be inspected or dumped below the encrypted boundary. Simulating a design with such IP requires -L secureip (and -L unisims_ver/unisim, simprims_ver, xpm), the IP's generated simulation output products (generate_target simulation) and, for third-party tools, a simulator version supported by the release (encryption keys are tool-specific). User RTL can be protected the same way with the encrypt Tcl command (IEEE 1735 with the vendor keys) before delivery.
tools.usage:
xelab -L unisims_ver -L secureip -L xpm -L <ip_library_from_the_generated_sim_scripts> glbl work.tb -s sim
# protect your own RTL for delivery
encrypt -key <keyfile> -lang verilog [glob ./deliver/*.v]
# IP simulation products
generate_target simulation [get_ips gtwizard_ultrascale_0]
export_ip_user_files -of_objects [get_ips gtwizard_ultrascale_0] -no_script -sync -force

parameters.name: -L secureip
parameters.description: Encrypted primitive models (GT, PCIe, etc.).

parameters.name: encrypt -key <file> -lang verilog|vhdl
parameters.description: Encrypt sources with the AMD (xilinx) public key so Vivado and supported simulators can consume them.

parameters.name: export_ip_user_files
parameters.description: Regenerates <project>.ip_user_files with the sim scripts and per-simulator library mapping.

tools.example:
# Typical failure: 'Library secureip not found' -> add -L secureip, or for Questa ensure compile_simlib included -library secureip
compile_simlib -simulator questa -family kintexuplus -language verilog -library secureip -library unisim -library simprim
tools.notes: Encrypted models cannot be traced with ltrace/ptrace or dumped internally; waveform access stops at the wrapper ports. Protected IP with time-limited (evaluation) licenses also stops toggling in hardware after the timeout, not in simulation.

tools.name: Mixed-language simulation (VHDL/Verilog/SystemVerilog boundaries)
tools.description: xsim (and the supported third-party simulators via Vivado's scripts) simulate mixed VHDL, Verilog and SystemVerilog hierarchies: a Verilog module can instantiate a VHDL entity and vice versa, with type mapping at the boundary (std_logic/std_logic_vector to wire/reg vectors, integer/natural to integer, generics of type integer/string/boolean/std_logic_vector to parameters), and VHDL-2008 features enabled per file with the file_type VHDL 2008 property (or xvhdl -2008). Restrictions: VHDL cannot see SystemVerilog interfaces, packages or classes, records/unconstrained arrays across the boundary are not supported, and Verilog parameters of real type are not passed into VHDL generics.
tools.usage:
set_property file_type {VHDL 2008} [get_files core.vhd]
xvhdl -2008 -work mylib core.vhd
xvlog -sv -work work tb_top.sv wrapper.v
xelab -L mylib work.tb_top -s mixed_sim     ;# libraries resolved through xsim.ini
# generic override across languages
xelab -generic_top "DATA_WIDTH=32" work.tb_top

parameters.name: file_type property
parameters.description: Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL, VHDL 2008, VHDL 2019 per source file (also controls synthesis parsing).

parameters.name: library property
parameters.description: Library a source is compiled into (default xil_defaultlib / work).

parameters.name: Type mapping
parameters.description: std_logic <-> 1-bit, std_logic_vector <-> vector, signed/unsigned <-> vector, integer <-> integer, boolean <-> 1-bit (see the UG900 mixed-language table for the exact rules).

tools.notes: Case sensitivity: Verilog names are case-sensitive, VHDL are not; Vivado matches ports case-insensitively at the boundary but two Verilog ports differing only in case cannot be bound from VHDL. Use SystemVerilog packages for SV<->SV type sharing and plain vectors at VHDL boundaries.

tools.name: XSim Waveform / Scope / Objects windows
tools.description: The simulation GUI layout that opens with launch_simulation (or xsim -gui): the Scope window shows the design hierarchy (instances, blocks, processes) and selecting a scope fills the Objects window with its signals, variables and constants (drag to the waveform or right-click Add to Wave Window / Log to Wave Database); the Waveform window displays logged signals with cursors, markers, groups, dividers, virtual buses, radix/analog display, zoom-to-cursor, search for value/transition (Find Value), Go To Time, and the Save Waveform Configuration button; the toolbar has Restart, Run All, Run For, Step, Break and Relaunch, mirrored by the Tcl commands. Breakpoints are set in the text editor gutter and hit lines are highlighted.
tools.usage: Flow Navigator > Simulation > Run Simulation > Run Behavioral Simulation; Window > Waveform / Scope / Objects; toolbar Run All (F3), Run For, Restart, Relaunch Simulation (key bindings in Tools > Settings > Shortcuts)

parameters.name: Objects window filters
parameters.description: Show only inputs/outputs/internal signals/constants/variables; search field.

parameters.name: Waveform right-click
parameters.description: Radix, Waveform Style (digital/analog), Signal Name Width, New Group/Divider/Virtual Bus, Show Drivers, Go To Source Code.

parameters.name: Cursor and markers
parameters.description: Main and secondary cursor with delta time readout; Add Marker button.

tools.example:
1. launch_simulation (the testbench top is set in Settings > Simulation)
2. Scope: expand tb_top > dut > u_fifo, select it; Objects: select wr_en, din, full; drag into Waveform
3. Right-click din > Radix > Hexadecimal; New Group 'write side'
4. Run For 2 us; Zoom Fit; add a marker at the first full assertion
5. File > Simulation Waveform > Save Configuration As... (tb_fifo.wcfg is added to sim_1)
tools.notes: Signals added after the simulation ran show no history unless log_all_signals (xsim.simulate.log_all_signals) was set; use Relaunch or Restart + Run. The Waveform window can also open a .wdb from a batch run (File > Simulation Waveform > Open Waveform Database).

tools.name: .wcfg / .wdb (waveform configuration and database)
tools.description: The two waveform files of xsim: .wcfg is an XML waveform configuration describing which objects are displayed, their order, groups, dividers, virtual buses, radixes, colours, markers and zoom state (saved by save_wave_config and reusable across runs and designs with matching names); .wdb is the binary waveform database holding the logged value changes of the simulation (written when log_wave / log_all_signals is used, named with xsim -wdb or defaulting to <top>_behav.wdb in the run directory) and can be reopened read-only with open_wave_database for post-mortem inspection. Neither is human-readable in a useful way except for editing signal paths in a .wcfg after a rename.
tools.usage:
save_wave_config ./layouts/tb_top.wcfg      ;# XML layout
xsim tb_sim -tclbatch run.tcl -wdb ./runs/tb_top_$seed.wdb
open_wave_database ./runs/tb_top_42.wdb
open_wave_config ./layouts/tb_top.wcfg

parameters.name: .wcfg
parameters.description: Add to the simulation fileset (add_files -fileset sim_1) so it opens automatically.

parameters.name: .wdb
parameters.description: Grows with logged signal count and run length; can reach gigabytes with log_wave -r on large designs.

tools.example:
# regression: keep the wdb only on failure
if {[catch {exec xsim tb_sim -R -wdb fail.wdb -onerror quit}]} { puts "kept fail.wdb for analysis" } else { file delete fail.wdb }
tools.notes: A .wcfg saved from a different design still loads; missing objects are flagged. .wdb files are release-specific (open with the same Vivado version that wrote them).

tools.name: Settings > Simulation dialog (Run Simulation menu)
tools.description: Project-level simulation settings dialog (Flow Navigator > Settings > Simulation, or Tools > Settings > Project Settings > Simulation): choose Target simulator, Simulator language (Mixed/Verilog/VHDL), Simulation set (sim_1 ...), Simulation top module name, Generate scripts only, Clean up simulation files, and the compiled library location; the Compilation, Elaboration, Simulation, Netlist and Advanced tabs expose the xsim.compile.*/xsim.elaborate.*/xsim.simulate.* properties (runtime, log all signals, debug level, more options, SAIF, SDF delay, netlist generation options such as unifast and process corner). The Run Simulation button's dropdown (Flow Navigator > Simulation) offers Run Behavioral, Post-Synthesis Functional/Timing and Post-Implementation Functional/Timing Simulation.
tools.usage: Flow Navigator > Settings > Simulation > tabs: Compilation | Elaboration | Simulation | Netlist | Advanced; Flow Navigator > Simulation > Run Simulation > Run Behavioral Simulation / Run Post-Synthesis Functional Simulation / Run Post-Synthesis Timing Simulation / Run Post-Implementation Functional Simulation / Run Post-Implementation Timing Simulation

parameters.name: Netlist tab
parameters.description: xsim.netlist.* options for post-synthesis/implementation: unifast library, process corner (slow/fast), write netlist with SDF, rename top.

parameters.name: Advanced tab
parameters.description: Include all design sources for simulation, enable incremental compilation, use custom xsim.ini/-L paths.

parameters.name: Simulation set / top
parameters.description: current_fileset -simset and the top property.

tools.example:
1. Settings > Simulation: Target simulator = Vivado Simulator, Simulation top = tb_top
2. Simulation tab: xsim.simulate.runtime = all, xsim.simulate.log_all_signals = true
3. OK; Run Simulation > Run Behavioral Simulation
4. Later: Run Post-Implementation Timing Simulation (the Netlist tab's SDF delay = sdfmax)
tools.notes: Each GUI change echoes the corresponding set_property on the fileset in the Tcl console. Settings are stored in the .xpr; export_simulation captures them into standalone scripts.
